title: From minimal informationally complete measurements to orthocentric simplices and back again
authors: Piotr Bereza, Wojciech Słomczyński, Anna Szymusiak
abstract: The reconstruction of unknown quantum states via minimal informationally complete measurements (MICs) is a cornerstone of quantum tomography. Although the statistical properties of these measurements are well-understood, their geometric structure has remained elusive. In this work, we establish a correspondence between the class of minimal $s$-tight informationally complete measurements, encompassing, among others, tight IC and morphophoric measurements, and the classical geometry of orthocentric simplices. In particular, we prove a three-way equivalence: a MIC is $s$-tight if and only if its measurement vectors, upon suitable rescaling, form the vertices of an acute orthocentric simplex with the orthocentre at the origin, and such simplices are precisely the homothetically self-dual ones. This geometric manifestation of operational ''tightness'' provides a bridge between the physical world and Euclidean geometry. Furthermore, the $s$-tight class is fully characterised by its measurement directions: the angles between them must be obtuse and satisfy a cross-ratio condition. We determine the space of admissible direction configurations: modulo rotations, every such configuration is encoded by a single probability vector, the ''skeleton'' of the measurement, together with an orientation class, so that the moduli space of $s$-tight MIC directions is $Δ^{\circ}_{d+1}\times\{\pm 1\}$. Conversely, every acute orthocentric simplex with the orthocentre at the origin can be anchored in the state space, generating a class of minimal $s$-tight IC measurements that contains exactly one tight IC measurement up to overall rescaling.
summary: This theoretical paper connects the operational concept of minimal informationally complete measurements in Generalized Probabilistic Theories to classical Euclidean geometry. It proves that these 'tight' measurements are characterized by their associated vectors forming an acute orthocentric simplex. This establishes a deep, quantifiable link between optimal physical measurement procedures and fundamental geometric structures.
main_problem: The paper establishes a deep geometric correspondence between minimal informationally complete measurements (MICs) in Generalized Probabilistic Theories (GPTs) and the classical geometry of acute orthocentric simplices.
main_result: It proves a three-way equivalence: an MIC is $s$-tight if and only if its rescaled measurement vectors form the vertices of an acute orthocentric simplex centered at the origin, which must also be homothetically self-dual.
method: The authors use intrinsic geometric approaches to GPTs, relating operational constraints (like 'tightness') to specific algebraic conditions on the measurement vectors ($\Psi$) and outcome probabilities ($c$).
model_or_system: The study is set within Generalized Probabilistic Theories (GPTs), which generalize quantum mechanics by defining states as a convex body $S$ in a vector space $V_0$. The focus is on minimal IC measurements, which require exactly $d+1$ outcomes.
key_observables: Measurement vectors ($\Psi$), outcome probabilities ($c$), and the resulting geometric structure (acute orthocentric simplex).
important_parameters: The dimension of the state space ($d+1$), the skeleton probability vector ($P \in \Delta^{\circ}_{d+1}$), and the scaling factor $A$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a finite-dimensional setting, relies on specific definitions for the fiducial scalar product $\langle x, y angle_{P,A}$, and makes assumptions about the structure of the GGPT (e.g., supra-duality).
figures_summary: Figure 1 conceptually illustrates states ($S$), measurement vectors ($\psi_j$), and how probabilities $c$ are determined via barycentric coordinates.
paper_structure: The paper develops from defining MICs in GGPTs, establishing the geometric link to orthocentric simplices through necessary conditions (obtuse angles, cross-ratio), culminating in the main equivalence theorem that parameterizes the space of such measurements by $\Delta^{\circ}_{d+1}$.
why_interesting: While not directly about AMO systems, this work provides a powerful mathematical framework for characterizing optimal measurement strategies in any physical theory (including quantum mechanics) purely through geometric constraints on the state space.
